summary: Mistral released Leanstral 1.5, a free Apache-2.0 licensed 119B-total/6B-active-parameter mixture-of-experts model specialized in formal verification and Lean 4 theorem proving, publishing weights on Hugging Face along with a free API and open-sourcing the FLTEval benchmark.

mechanisms.reason: The model's sparse mixture-of-experts architecture (6B active of 119B total parameters) and stated per-problem cost figures show lower compute/cost per solved problem than comparable provers.
mechanisms.quote: On PutnamBench, it edges out Seed-Prover 1.5 high by 7 problems at far lower cost: about $4 per problem, against an estimated $300 or more for Seed-Prover

mechanisms.reason: The MoE architecture requires storing 119B total parameters despite only 6B active per token, and test-time reasoning runs to millions of tokens, both increasing memory footprint per system.
mechanisms.quote: a free Apache-2.0 licensed model with 119B total and only 6B active parameters

practices.reason: A specialized model with stated benchmark gains in formal proof reasoning, code verification, and long-horizon agentic proof engineering is worth evaluating for teams doing formal verification work, though it is not a general-purpose capability upgrade most teams depend on.
practices.quote: Leanstral 1.5 saturates miniF2F, solves 587/672 PutnamBench problems, and achieves a new state-of-the-art of %87 on FATE-H and 34% on FATE-X

practices.reason: The lab open-sourced the FLTEval benchmark based on real pull requests, giving teams a transferable instrument for measuring practical proof-engineering capability.
practices.quote: With this release, we also fully open source FLTEval .

practices.reason: The code agent environment with file editing, bash commands, language-server introspection, and context compaction is a concrete long-horizon agent scaffolding pattern with stated test-time scaling results, but is specific to the Lean proving setting and would need adaptation elsewhere.
practices.quote: it edits files, runs bash commands, and uses the Lean language server to inspect goals, errors, and type information in real time
